config.title: Build contract tests for API responses

intro.title: Build contract tests for API responses
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple contract test to verify that an API response matches an expected structure. You will learn the core concept of contract testing, which ensures that an API's output adheres to a predefined format or 'contract.' The main technologies involved are Node.js, the built-in 'assert' module for validation, and a mock API response. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to write tests that catch breaking changes in APIs.
intro.usecase: Contract tests for API responses are essential in real-world applications like e-commerce platforms where multiple services (product catalog, inventory, payment) must communicate reliably. When a frontend dashboard displays user order history, it depends on consistent response structures from the order service API. Without contract tests, backend changes could break the dashboard's ability to parse order dates or amounts, causing display errors for users. These tests ensure that API updates don't unexpectedly break integrations between microservices or between mobile apps and their backend APIs.

objectives: Initialize a testing framework and assertion library for Node.js API contract tests
Construct a mock API response that matches a predefined contract schema
Implement contract validation by comparing actual API responses against expected structures
Configure test suites to handle different HTTP status codes and response types
Manipulate test data to simulate edge cases and error scenarios in API contracts
Integrate contract tests into a continuous integration workflow script
Apply contract testing principles to validate API endpoints for consistency

steps.title: Import required testing libraries
steps.instruction: Import the required testing libraries: assert from 'assert', supertest from 'supertest', and mocha hooks (describe, it).
steps.hint: Use the 'require' statement to import each library. For mocha hooks, you can destructure them from the global object or import them directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The testing libraries are imported and ready to use for contract testing.
successCriteria: assert is imported from 'assert', supertest is imported from 'supertest', and describe and it are imported from 'mocha'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required libraries, but not all. Make sure to import assert, supertest, and the mocha hooks (describe, it).
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import assert from 'assert', supertest from 'supertest', and describe and it from 'mocha'.

steps.title: Create a test file structure
steps.instruction: Create a describe block for API contract tests. Use the describe function to define a test suite with the description 'API Contract Tests'.
steps.hint: The describe function takes two arguments: a string description and a callback function containing your tests.
steps.seedCode:
// Import required testing libraries here

// Create a describe block for API contract tests
steps.expectedOutcome: A test suite structure is created with a describe block that will contain your API contract tests.
successCriteria: The code contains a describe block with the description 'API Contract Tests' and an empty callback function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a complete describe block with both the description string and callback function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test suite structure isn't quite right. Remember to use the describe function with 'API Contract Tests' as the description and an empty callback function.

steps.title: Initialize the API server for testing
steps.instruction: Import your Express app and create a supertest instance with it.
steps.hint: Use the supertest library to create a test agent that can make HTTP requests to your Express application.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test file will have a supertest instance ready to make HTTP requests to your Express application.
successCriteria: Express app is imported and a supertest instance is created with it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported both the Express app and supertest, then created the instance.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've imported your Express app and used supertest to create a test instance with it.

steps.title: Define the first contract test case
steps.instruction: Inside the describe block, create an 'it' test case that describes testing the GET /users endpoint contract.
steps.hint: Use the 'it' function from Jest to define a test case. The first argument should be a string describing what the test does.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test case structure is created with a descriptive message about the GET /users endpoint.
successCriteria: An 'it' block is defined with a string describing the GET /users endpoint contract test.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the 'it' function with a descriptive string about the GET /users endpoint.
steps.feedbackWrong: create an 'it' test case inside the describe block that describes testing the GET /users endpoint contract.

steps.title: Make the API request in the test
steps.instruction: Inside your existing test case, use the supertest instance to make a GET request to the '/users' endpoint.
steps.hint: Call the .get() method on your supertest instance with the endpoint path as an argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Making a GET request with supertest
const response = await request.get('/api/data');
steps.expectedOutcome: The test case now contains code to make a GET request to the /users endpoint using supertest.
successCriteria: The test case includes a supertest GET request to '/users' endpoint.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some request code, but make sure it's a GET request to exactly '/users'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test case doesn't contain the expected API request. Try adding: const response = await request.get('/users');

steps.title: Assert the response status code
steps.instruction: Inside the test case, add an assertion that the response status code equals 200.
steps.hint: Use the expect function with response.status and the .toBe matcher to check for status code 200.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test case now includes an assertion that verifies the API returns a 200 status code.
successCriteria: The test case contains expect(response.status).toBe(200) after the API request.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using expect with response.status and .toBe(200) exactly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The assertion is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using expect(response.status).toBe(200) inside the test case.

steps.title: Assert the response content type
steps.instruction: Inside your existing test case, add an assertion that checks the response's Content-Type header equals 'application/json'.
steps.hint: Use the expect() function with response.headers['content-type'] or response.type.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test will verify the API returns JSON content by checking the Content-Type header.
successCriteria: The test case includes an assertion that the response's Content-Type header is 'application/json'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your assertion specifically checks for 'application/json' in the Content-Type header.
steps.feedbackWrong: The assertion for Content-Type is missing or incorrect. Use expect() to verify the header value.

steps.title: Add a test for POST endpoint contract
steps.instruction: Add a second 'it' test case after your existing test to test the POST /users endpoint with sample user data.
steps.hint: Create a new 'it' block that makes a POST request with a sample user object and asserts the response.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have two test cases: one for GET /users and one for POST /users.
successCriteria: A second 'it' block is added that tests POST /users with sample data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a test case, but make sure it's for POST /users and includes sample data in the request body.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint test case is missing or incomplete. Add an 'it' block that tests POST /users.

steps.title: Run the contract tests
steps.instruction: Execute your contract tests by running the test command in your terminal.
steps.hint: Use the npm script you configured in your package.json or run mocha directly with the test file path.
steps.expectedOutcome: All contract tests pass, verifying the API responses match the expected structure and behavior.
successCriteria: Tests are executed and all assertions pass without errors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Tests ran but some assertions failed. Check your test expectations match the actual API response structure and status codes.
steps.feedbackWrong: Unable to run tests. Ensure your test command is correctly configured and the test file exists.
